newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FOCUS-Aircraft sales help SIA earnings.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Aircraft sales help SIA earnings.

text.p: Singapore Airlines Ltd (SIA) posted a modest 0.6 percent increase in its 1997 group earnings on Friday to Singapore $1,032 million (US$716.7 million), up from S$1,025 million the year before.
Deputy chairman and chief operating officer Cheong Choong Kong said in statement said the national carriers' bottom line had been helped by a surplus from the sale of aircraft.
"It was a disappointing performance, redeemed partly by our ability to sell surplus aircraft at a profit," he said.
Cheong blamed the weak performance on high aviation fuel costs, a strong Singapore dollar and sluggish economies in some of its major markets including Japan.
The flat earnings reflected market expectations.

"It is largely in line what the market had expected. The operating profit was just slightly lower than expected and surplus from aircraft sales was higher," said Sim Chey Hoon, investment analyst with Merrill Lynch.
Operating profit from SIA's core airline operations fell 13.6 percent to Singapore $653 million while revenue rose by 4.3 percent to S$6,519 million.
SIA said that if the exchange rate of the Singapore dollar against major currencies had been unchanged from the preceeding year, revenue would have been S$185 million higher.
Expenditure went up by 6.7 percent to S$5,866 million.
SIA said the higher price of fuel alone added S$153 million to expenditure.
The airline's pretax profit was higher after accounting for a surplus of S$159 million from the sale of surplus aircraft and spares. In the previous year, SIA had no aircraft sales.
Overall yield went down 4.6 percent t0 66.5 cents per load tonne-kilometre with passenger and cargo yields slipping 3.9 percent and 4.6 percent respectively.

SIA said the fall in yields was due to a 3.6 percent appreciation of the Singapore dollar against a basket of major foreign currencies, a drop in local yields due to competition and a higher proportion of cargo carriage.
On prospects, the carrier said overall capacity for 1997-1998 was expected to increase by nine percent with available passenger capacity growing seven percent and cargo capacity by 10 percent.

Passenger yields were expected to remain under pressure due to competition and the strong Singapore dollar but cargo yields were expected to improve with a recent pick up in demand for cargo space and an expected recovery in electronics exports.
SIA said it was proposing a bonus dividend of 7.5 cents per share to celebrate its 50th anniversary.
Sim said she expected SIA to post better earnings growth in the current year due lower fuel costs and better management of yields.
"But it will not exceed 10 percent," she said.
-- Singapore newsroom (65 8703199)
